ORIGINAL USMLE-STYLE PRACTICE

Vitamin K recycling

A laboratory studies hepatocytes exposed to warfarin. Newly produced coagulation proteins show impaired gamma-carboxylation and reduced calcium-dependent function. Which inhibited process most directly explains this effect on protein maturation in the liver?

  1. Regeneration of reduced vitamin K
  2. Proteolytic conversion of plasminogen
  3. Binding of thrombin to fibrin
  4. Release of ADP from platelets
  5. Synthesis of antithrombin protein
Answer and explanation

Regeneration of reduced vitamin K

Warfarin inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase and limits reduced vitamin K availability.

Option explanations

Regeneration of reduced vitamin K: Warfarin inhibits vitamin K epoxide reductase and limits reduced vitamin K availability.

Proteolytic conversion of plasminogen: Plasminogen activation is a fibrinolytic process.

Binding of thrombin to fibrin: Thrombin-fibrin binding is not the hepatic target.

Release of ADP from platelets: Platelet secretion does not explain impaired carboxylation.

Synthesis of antithrombin protein: Antithrombin synthesis is not the main warfarin target.
